Statement-I: Nitrogen in pyridine cannot be estimated by Kjeldahl's method.
Statement-II: Nitrogen in pyridine changes to ammonium sulphate when heated with conc. $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ in Kjeldahl's method.
Read the above given statements and choose the correct answer from the given options.

questions.explanation_text: Statement-I is true. In Kjeldahl’s method, the nitrogen present in an organic compound is converted into ammonium sulphate, $(\text{NH}_{4})_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ , by heating with concentrated $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ . But this method does not work for all nitrogen-containing compounds. It fails for compounds in which nitrogen is present in certain special forms, such as: nitro compounds azo compounds diazo compounds heterocyclic compounds like pyridine In pyridine, nitrogen is part of the aromatic ring. This nitrogen does not get converted into ammonium sulphate on heating with concentrated $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ . So Statement-II is false. Hence, the correct answer is: $\text{Option A}$ Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
questions.explanation_html:
Statement-I is true.

In Kjeldahl’s method, the nitrogen present in an organic compound is converted into ammonium sulphate, $(\text{NH}_{4})_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ , by heating with concentrated $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ .

But this method does not work for all nitrogen-containing compounds. It fails for compounds in which nitrogen is present in certain special forms, such as:

  • nitro compounds

  • azo compounds

  • diazo compounds

  • heterocyclic compounds like pyridine

In pyridine, nitrogen is part of the aromatic ring. This nitrogen does not get converted into ammonium sulphate on heating with concentrated $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ .

So Statement-II is false.

Hence, the correct answer is:

$\text{Option A}$

Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.explanation_text: (a) The first compound is 2-butanol. It is an aliphatic alcohol, which means the $-\text{OH}$ group is attached to an alkyl chain. Alcohols give a red colour with ceric ammonium nitrate solution. So, (a) matches with (iii). (b) $\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{5}\text{NH}_{2}$ is aniline. It is a primary aromatic amine. Aniline gives the azo dye test. In this test, it forms a diazonium salt with nitrous acid, and then couples with $\beta$ -naphthol to give an orange-red dye. So, (b) matches with (ii). (c) $\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CHO}$ is propanal. It contains the aldehyde group $-\text{CHO}$ . Aldehydes give Tollen's reagent test and form a silver mirror. So, (c) matches with (iv). (d) The second compound is phenol. Phenols give a violet colour with neutral $\text{FeCl}_{3}$ solution. So, (d) matches with (i). The correct matching is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
questions.explanation_html:
(a) The first compound is 2-butanol. It is an aliphatic alcohol, which means the $-\text{OH}$ group is attached to an alkyl chain. Alcohols give a red colour with ceric ammonium nitrate solution. So, (a) matches with (iii).

(b) $\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{5}\text{NH}_{2}$ is aniline. It is a primary aromatic amine. Aniline gives the azo dye test. In this test, it forms a diazonium salt with nitrous acid, and then couples with $\beta$ -naphthol to give an orange-red dye. So, (b) matches with (ii).

(c) $\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CHO}$ is propanal. It contains the aldehyde group $-\text{CHO}$ . Aldehydes give Tollen's reagent test and form a silver mirror. So, (c) matches with (iv).

(d) The second compound is phenol. Phenols give a violet colour with neutral $\text{FeCl}_{3}$ solution. So, (d) matches with (i).

The correct matching is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
